clue.text: Instant support

definitions.meaning: an instant is a moment, a very short span of time
to back a motion or a speaker is to give support

explanation.definitionFit: A moment is a tiny span of time, and backing a proposal formally is a word meaning to support it.

clue.text: An extract from The Prisoner of Zenda? Not likely!

definitions.text: An extract from The Prisoner of Zenda?
definitions.meaning: The Prisoner of Zenda was written by Anthony Hope, so a part of it is a portion of his writing
a scornful exclamation meaning there is no chance at all

explanation.walkthrough: The novel's author, Anthony Hope, is the key: a piece of his book is a bit of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope wrote the novel, so a portion of it is a bit of that author; as an idiom the phrase scoffs at any chance of success.

clue.text: Gold lined cabinet for a naval officer

indicators.note: the gold forms a lining, sitting inside the cabinet word

parts.note: a commode is a cabinet or chest of drawers
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A sailor's chest has been fitted with a gilded lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lined' says the gold forms the lining; OR is the heraldic word for gold, and the cabinet is a commode, a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in the navy above captain, held by a senior sea officer.

clue.text: Usual amount and not a large number

parts.note: nor is the word meaning and not
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Something is the standard quantity rather than a vast one.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard or typical quantity, the expected level of output.

clue.text: Cadet due for promotion, having been taught well

indicators.note: promotion here means moving the letters up and about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A military trainee is about to rise in rank after thorough schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for promotion' rearranges CADETDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled thoroughly has received a good learning.

clue.text: The depth one may sink to as a sa

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'The depth one may sink to as a sa', cut off mid-word; the scan is absent and a search of the exact text found nothing, so the ending is unknown.
annotationWithheld.clue: The depth one may sink to as a sa

clue.text: I don't understand it, the bookie's stopped taking bets

definitions.meaning: something wholly incomprehensible to a person
a betting book that has been shut so no more wagers are accepted

explanation.definitionFit: A mystery to someone is an idiom about being unreadable; a bookmaker's ledger that is shut takes no more stakes.

clue.text: Feverish activity in temples?

parts.note: temples are not places of worship but the sides of the head, where a pulse is felt beating during a fever or headache

explanation.walkthrough: 'temples' suggests churches, but means the sides of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pounding pulse is felt at the sides of the head during fever.

clue.text: Run out on the sand

definitions.meaning: to run out on someone is to abandon them
a vast sandy wasteland like the Sahara

explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to leave them in the lurch; an arid sandy region like the Sahara is the other sense.

clue.text: Egg-how nice it can be scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled, like eggs, signals the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook marvels at how good an egg can be when scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be scrambled' rearranges NICEIT; 'Egg' is the verb, as in egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or provoke them.

clue.text: Roman made discordant notes

indicators.note: discordant means jarring and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman composer produced some jarring musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discordant' rearranges ROMANMADE; 'notes' is written memos, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin-derived word for written reminders or memos.

clue.text: Imagined monsters, rose about midnight, upset

indicators.note: the flower's letters go around the middle letter of the night
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the middle of the word night is G

explanation.surface: At midnight someone dreams of monsters while a rose is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts G around by ROSE; 'upset' then rearranges those five letters. 'midnight' is the middle letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy-tale giants who eat people, creatures of the imagination.

clue.text: Eye-catching gadget

parts.note: in dressmaking an eye is a small loop, and the device that catches it is its partner fastener

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-catching' seems to mean striking but literally means catching an eye, the loop of a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved metal fastener on clothing catches its loop partner, the eye.

clue.text: Where they are unlikely to serve doubles?

definitions.text: Where they are unlikely to serve doubles?

parts.words: Where they are unlikely to serve doubles?
parts.note: a double is a big measure of spirits, and also a pair of people; a venue for unattached people pairs badly with couples

explanation.walkthrough: 'serve doubles' sounds like tennis or double measures of spirits; the twist is couples.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or club frequented by unattached people looking to meet a partner.

clue.text: One who is deep, not silly

definitions.text: One who is deep, not silly

parts.words: One who is deep, not silly
parts.note: in cricket, deep and silly are fielding positions far from and very close to the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'deep' positions are near the boundary and 'silly' ones are right beside the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket player stationed far from the wicket, near the boundary.

clue.text: Possible purse of plenty

definitions.note: used as an adjective, meaning abundant

indicators.note: possible here suggests a possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A purse might hold a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges PURSEOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant or lavish, existing in great quantity.

clue.text: One may take battle formation

indicators.note: formation means forming the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: Troops line up in battle formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges BATTLE; the definition is something you swallow, a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is something a patient may swallow.

clue.text: Away of looking for respect

parts.note: a parade-ground order to turn the head as a salute to a dignitary

explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' is an OCR join of 'A way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command to turn the head toward a reviewing officer as a mark of honour.

clue.text: Such ladies' shoes were impressive

parts.note: impressive literally: their narrow heels left dents, impressions, in floors

explanation.walkthrough: 'impressive' means making impressions: such pointed heels famously dented floors.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin high heel on women's footwear, named after a slim dagger.

clue.text: A little lower

parts.note: lower here is one who lows, moos, and a little one is a young cow

explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'more low' but one who lows, that is moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow that has not calved, a small creature that moos.

clue.text: Set of teeth chatter uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably means wildly, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone's teeth chatter uncontrollably from the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrollably' rearranges CHATTER; the teeth are a toothed mechanical bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed bar or wheel with a pawl, a mechanism of cogs.

clue.text: Remarkable novel, it is intensely passionate

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked out afresh, signals rearranging

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises an outstanding book full of fierce emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' rearranges NOVEL and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce or extreme in feeling, as in raging emotion.

clue.text: Watches through the night

parts.note: watches are periods of keeping awake, kept all night

explanation.definitionFit: Periods of staying awake to keep watch or pray during the night.

clue.text: At university, go for a result

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
a go or attempt is a shot

explanation.surface: A student goes all out for good grades.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: Part of centre-page spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine has a section in its central double-page feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges CENTREPAGE; a centre-page spread is a magazine's middle pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion or share of the whole, expressed per hundred.

clue.text: Kingdom not fancied by many

parts.note: not imagined, so genuine
M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many

explanation.surface: A domain unloved by the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's domain, a country ruled by a king.

clue.text: Large number leave lesson for exam

indicators.note: leave means go away from, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson
M is a thousand in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Many pupils skip class to sit a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes M out of MORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language exam taken by speaking.

clue.text: It's hotly tipped so raise the stake

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A favourite tip in a bet, so a gambler increases their stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns ANTE upwards; 'hotly tipped' describes a volcano with a fiery summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sicilian volcano whose summit, its tip, is hot.

clue.text: Found out, caught and tried

definitions.meaning: a court case that has been judged

explanation.definitionFit: News is learned by listening, a sound is picked up by ear, and a legal case is considered by a judge.

clue.text: Keep getting drunk? Now hang on!

parts.note: to keep is to hold
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to keep a grip as they get tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A command to grip firmly and not let go.

clue.text: it's rash returning yet possesses worth

definitions.note: describes rash boldness, a noun quality

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the worth word inside it
returning means the word yet is read backwards

parts.note: merit means worth

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a rash act may still turn out worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the clue's own word yet around to give TEY; 'possesses' says that turned word holds the worth word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity or reckless boldness, the quality of acting rashly.

clue.text: A beating that leaves marks on the skin

definitions.meaning: a rhythmic drumming, as for a military signal

definitions.text: that leaves marks on the skin
definitions.meaning: an inked design pricked into the skin

explanation.definitionFit: A drum signal or military display, and an inked permanent design on the body.
